message.reasoning:
I am playing as player p4 (grok-4.7) in this Monopoly turn.

I own a complete yellow monopoly. Building one house on each property costs $450, leaving $9 cash.

Even building is required. p3 has light blue hotels and $2081. p1 owns all four railroads and $430. p2 has utilities and $464 with one GOOJF.

Even building is required. One house on each yellow costs $450 and leaves only $9 cash. That is extremely risky. A future rent or tax could bankrupt me or force selling houses at half price.

Light blue hotels cost $550 to $600. I need cash buffers to survive them. If a hotel hits, selling houses at half price and mortgaging would be terrible EV. Building just one house may not be legal under even-building rules.

Uneven building may be allowed. A one-house difference is standard in Monopoly. One house costs $150 and leaves $309. Two houses cost $300 and leave $159. Three houses cost $450 and leave only $9. The question is whether that rent increase justifies the risk.

I just bought Mediterranean Avenue and passed GO. The next players to move are p1, p2, and p3 before I roll again.

p1 is on Income Tax (space 4). The yellow properties are at spaces 26 through 28. That is a distance of 22 to 24 spaces. A single roll cannot reach them. p1 will not land on yellow this turn.

p2 is on Boardwalk (space 39).

p2 cannot reach the yellows from Boardwalk. p3 is on Oriental Avenue, which is too far away for a single roll. Nobody can land on my yellows before my next turn. Building houses now would be a pure cash drain with no rent generated until after I roll again.

Houses would sit idle for an entire round of opponent moves with no rent collected. The real danger is that I might land on a hotel during my own roll and need the cash or mortgage capacity to survive it.

I will roll from Mediterranean next turn. Oriental, Vermont, and Connecticut are five, seven, and eight spaces away. That gives a 15 in 36 chance of landing on a light blue hotel. Oriental and Vermont each pay $550. Connecticut pays $600. I have $459 cash.

Mortgaging Park Place and New York Avenue covers a $550 hotel hit, leaving $34. A $600 hotel would still leave a $16 shortfall. If I build one house first, cash drops to $309. That same $550 hit leaves $34, but a $600 hit leaves only $13. I am checking the mortgage values of my yellows to see if they can cover the gap.

Mortgaging a yellow property with houses requires selling all houses on that color group first. A single house on each yellow would cost $75 to sell before mortgaging. That would break the monopoly and eliminate double rent.

Building one house and surviving a $600 hotel would leave only $59 after selling the house and mortgaging two properties. That is a net loss of $75 from the $150 build. Without building, the same hit leaves $134, keeping the monopoly intact. The 42% chance of hitting a hotel makes building negative EV because no rent is collected before that roll.

I am weighing other roll outcomes. A roll of 6 lands on Chance. A roll of 4 hits the Reading railroad and costs $200. A roll of 3 hits Income Tax for $200. A roll of 2 lands on Baltic, but that property is split between me and p3 so the base rent is only $4.

These risks make building houses even more dangerous. I should not build.

I also noticed p1 wants New York Avenue to complete an orange monopoly. I must never give it to them. They already own four railroads and could mortgage those to build houses.

I rejected p1's Boardwalk, Reading, and $100 offer for New York Avenue. That would arm them with a second lethal set.

A dark blue trade is now under consideration. Unmortgaging Boardwalk costs about $193. Each house on dark blue costs $200. That makes the trade expensive.

I cannot afford to unmortgage Boardwalk and build dark blue houses while still surviving light blue hotels. I have no other valuable properties to offer p1, since Mediterranean is worthless to them and selling the yellow monopoly would be suicide. p2 has almost a pink set but lacks States, which p3 owns.

Selling the yellow monopoly to p2 would arm them with a new threat, since they already have utilities and $464. The only other trade under consideration is getting Boardwalk from p1 without giving up New York Avenue.

I cannot trade New York Avenue or Park Place to p1. I will not give up Mediterranean Avenue to p3 either, since that would complete their brown monopoly and deny me the strategic advantage. p2 has no green properties for me to acquire. Completing a green set would require giving up too much.
